newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan must mull steps on impact of low rates - govt.
newsitem.headline: Japan must mull steps on impact of low rates - govt.

text.p: Chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a parliamentary budget committee meeting on Wednesday that Japan needs to consider measures to deal with the adverse impact that low interest rates have on people's incomes.
He made the remarks in response to a question about the effect that Japan's low interest rates had on people's incomes.

"The only thing that Japan can be proud of in the rough wave of internationalisation is its extra-low interest rates. On the other hand, it means Japan lags behind in internationalisation. I think in the near future Japan will undergo rough waves and I think it is necessary to consider measures to cope with that."
Kajiyama has previously suggested the need for measures to help those who live on interest rate income and are suffering in the current low interest rate environment.
He has also said Japanese banks are falling behind in the globalisation of the banking business and therefore they cannot tolerate a rise in interest rates.
